meta.title: Canada munitions and UXO sites (builder dataset)
meta.timezone_note: Dates and 'last checked' values are recorded in America/Phoenix (UTC-7) calendar dates unless a source gives another zone.
meta.builder_note: Thor's builder auto-loads this file for the Canada section at dangerousmunitionsnearme.com/canada/. It uses the same site-object schema as data/sites.json, plus province (with state set to the same province/territory/coast code for builder compatibility), coord_precision, coord_source, and optional dnd_site_id / site_id_primary / site_id_secondary. U.S. EPA-only fields are present but blank or false.
meta.companion_official_extract: data/canada_uxo.json and data/canada_uxo.csv are the unchanged official-inventory extract (no inferred coordinates) and remain the attribution copy of the Open Government XLSX.
meta.inclusion_rule: Every official English XLSX row from National Defence's Unexploded Explosive Ordnance (UXO) Sites in Canada dataset is included as sector legacy_uxo (854 records). Additional active or proposed DND ranges, training areas, demolition/EOD areas, and ammunition depots are added as sector dnd only when a primary Government of Canada source documents them. Contractor or industrial energetics disposal sites are added as sector contractor only when a primary Government of Canada source documents them; none were added in this pass.
meta.coordinate_policy: The official UXO XLSX and the DND locations page do not publish coordinates. Approximate latitude and longitude are added only from an official Government of Canada geographic source, principally the Natural Resources Canada Canadian Geographical Names Database (CGNDB / geonames API). A point is recorded only when there is a unique official exact-name populated-place match in that province (CITY, TOWN, or VILG preferred; HAM/UNP/IR if no core settlement; MUN1 only if no settlement type exists). Multiple same-name places at different coordinates are left blank; this draft never chooses among them. Water-body, offshore, wreck, and dump-site names are left blank unless an official source gives coordinates for that site. Active DND records use a unique official CGNDB military or populated-place feature for the named installation or training area. All such points are coord_precision=place_name_approx (official named-feature points, not surveyed footprints). coord_precision=exact is reserved for a published official coordinate of the site itself (for example a Federal Contaminated Sites Inventory point for a named range); none were used in this pass. EC and WC records are queried without a province filter and accepted only if a unique populated place exists in all of Canada.
meta.verification_policy: Legacy UXO records are 'partly verified': the official inventory identity, name, province/coast code, and status are confirmed from the Open Government XLSX, but the published file does not give a surveyed location and this draft does not invent one. Active DND records are 'partly verified': official identity and the cited facts are confirmed from retrieved Government of Canada pages, but inventories, exact footprints, and some operational details are not in those pages.
meta.source_exclusions: This draft does not cite NYT, CNN, MSNBC/MS NOW, Fox News, Snopes, or PolitiFact.
meta.attribution: Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence – Canada.
meta.attribution_note: Information Provider: National Defence / His Majesty the King in right of Canada, and Natural Resources Canada for CGNDB coordinates. This tracker is not endorsed by the Government of Canada. Official symbols of the Information Provider are not used.
meta.public_comments_note: Optional public_comment_* fields are reserved for official consultations that are open at last_checked. IAAC registries checked on 2026-11-23, including 90236 (Shearwater proposed EOD range; comments closed 2026-03-10, assessment still in progress) and 90825 (Valcartier Combat Course Phase 2 / Termoli Range; comments closed 2026-10-27, assessment still in progress), were not open. No open official comment period was written into these fields.
coverage_gaps: The official UXO XLSX uses province/coast codes EC and WC, which are not expanded here because an official definition was not retrieved. There is no NT row in the official file. The DND locations webpage checked earlier on 2026-11-23 listed 853 IDs and omitted AB900-001 / 0539-X001 (Airdrie - Bombing Range); the XLSX has 854 unique IDs and all are included.
Coordinates remain blank for official names that are offshore dumps, wrecks, or water bodies, and for place names with no unique official CGNDB match.

National Defence reported 1,971 Federal Contaminated Sites Inventory entries in a 21 November 2024 briefing (1,221 closed; 107 high priority). This file does not import that inventory wholesale; many FCSI records are fuel, PFAS, or other contamination unrelated to ranges or energetics disposal.

No contractor or industrial energetics disposal site was added, because a primary Government of Canada source documenting a current contractor disposal or OB/OD operation was not retrieved in this pass. Historical industrial names that already appear in the official UXO inventory (for example Georgian Bay - Nobel Explosives Plant) remain legacy_uxo records.

Debert is documented through official legacy UXO rows (four of them deepened) rather than as a separate current CAF base, because a current official unit page confirming an active Debert range was not retrieved.
The four CFADs named in the May 2018 ammunition audit are Angus, Bedford, Dundurn, and Rocky Point; only Dundurn is added as a notable site in this pass.
meta.data_note: Do not mix these records into the U.S. data/sites.json file. Do not edit site/ or run a site build or publish from this pass. Keep data/canada_uxo.json and data/canada_uxo.csv unchanged as the official-extract companions.

sites.name: Airdrie - Bombing Range
sites.branch: Department of National Defence (UXO Legacy Sites inventory)
sites.coordinate_source: NRCan Canadian Geographical Names Database (CGNDB) official feature IAQFR (Airdrie, CITY). Place-name approximation for the uniquely matched named place in the official site name; not a surveyed UXO footprint.
sites.coordinate_method: Unique official CGNDB populated-place or municipality feature for the place name parsed from the official site name; accepted only when a single exact-name match (or unique CITY/TOWN/VILG, or unique MUN1 if no settlement type exists) is official in that province. Multiple same-name places at different coordinates are left blank.
sites.notes: Official DND UXO Legacy Sites record copied from the English Open Government XLSX. current_status is the official DND Status field. Verification is 'partly verified' because the official record is confirmed but the inventory does not publish a surveyed location; coordinates, when present, are an official CGNDB point for a uniquely matched named place, not the site footprint. Closed official status can be administrative and may be reopened; DND states that no technology guarantees all UXO will be found.

sites.name: Medicine Hat - Airport
sites.branch: Department of National Defence (UXO Legacy Sites inventory)
sites.coordinate_source: NRCan Canadian Geographical Names Database (CGNDB) official feature IAIUC (Medicine Hat, CITY). Place-name approximation for the uniquely matched named place in the official site name; not a surveyed UXO footprint.
sites.coordinate_method: Unique official CGNDB populated-place or municipality feature for the place name parsed from the official site name; accepted only when a single exact-name match (or unique CITY/TOWN/VILG, or unique MUN1 if no settlement type exists) is official in that province. Multiple same-name places at different coordinates are left blank.
sites.notes: Official DND UXO Legacy Sites record copied from the English Open Government XLSX. current_status is the official DND Status field. Verification is 'partly verified' because the official record is confirmed but the inventory does not publish a surveyed location; coordinates, when present, are an official CGNDB point for a uniquely matched named place, not the site footprint. Closed official status can be administrative and may be reopened; DND states that no technology guarantees all UXO will be found.

This record is one of a cluster of official DND UXO Legacy Sites named for Debert, Nova Scotia. In the official English XLSX, Debert - Main Site (NS900-075) is Assessment Complete; Debert - Explosives Demolition Area (NS900-076), Debert - Belmont Range (NS900-077), and Debert - Staples Brook Range (NS900-082) are Risk Mitigation Ongoing. Other Debert-named rows are Assessment Complete or In Assessment. Coordinates, when present, are the official NRCan CGNDB point for the unique unincorporated place Debert (CAJDV), not a surveyed footprint of each sub-site. CGNDB also records a separately named military feature 'Debert Range' (CAACB) at 45.442584, -63.473811; that point is not copied onto every Debert UXO row because the official inventory does not assign coordinates to individual records. An archived 2012–13 National Defence installations list named 'Canadian Forces Base Halifax Detachment Debert'; that archived listing is not treated as proof of a current CAF training base, and no current official CAF unit page for an active Debert range was retrieved in this pass, so Debert is documented here as legacy UXO rather than as a separate active DND site.

sites.name: 5 CDSB Gagetown / Gagetown Range and Training Area
sites.branch: Canadian Army / Department of National Defence
sites.coordinate_source: NRCan Canadian Geographical Names Database (CGNDB) official feature DBDXI (Gagetown Range and Training Area, MIL). Official named-feature point; not a surveyed installation or range footprint.
sites.coordinate_method: Official CGNDB military or populated-place feature uniquely named for this installation or training area.
sites.known_energetics: Official pages describe an active range and training area used for Army individual and collective training, including schools of the Combat Training Centre. An IAAC project description for a proposed EOD range at 12 Wing Shearwater states that live ordnance and white phosphorus munitions from Fleet Diving Unit Atlantic are currently transported on public roads to 5 CDSB Gagetown for disposal. This draft does not have a current item-level inventory of munitions at Gagetown.
sites.current_status: Active Canadian Army support base and range/training area. The official base page says 5 CDSB Gagetown opened in 1958 as a training facility and has an 1,100 square km training area. The main garrison is in Oromocto. As of the IAAC 90236 page checked on 2026-11-23, Fleet Diving Unit Atlantic still sends live ordnance and white phosphorus munitions to Gagetown for disposal. No open IAAC public-comment period for Gagetown was found on that date.

notable_incidents.description: National Defence’s Agent Orange investigations page states that for three days in June 1966, Agent Orange, Agent Purple, Agent White, and other herbicides were sprayed by the U.S. military at 5 CDSB Gagetown, with Canada’s permission, to test their effectiveness for vegetation management. The page says these 1966 and 1967 tests are the only known instances in which Agent Orange was tested on CAF property.
notable_incidents.summary: National Defence’s Agent Orange investigations page states that for three days in June 1966, Agent Orange, Agent Purple, Agent White, and other herbicides were sprayed by the U.S. military at 5 CDSB Gagetown, with Canada’s permission, to test their effectiveness for vegetation management. The page says these 1966 and 1967 tests are the only known instances in which Agent Orange was tested on CAF property.

notable_incidents.description: The same official page states that the U.S. military sprayed Agent Orange, Agent Purple, Agent White, and other herbicides at 5 CDSB Gagetown for four days in June 1967. It says the barrels were transported to the base by the U.S. military and records indicate they returned to the U.S. once testing was completed in 1967. It also states there is no evidence Agent Orange barrels were disposed of at the base, and that no barrels of Agent Orange have been found at Base Gagetown to date.

notable_incidents.description: DND, with Veterans Affairs Canada, Health Canada and other departments, began a 2005–2007 fact-finding investigation of herbicide testing and use at Base Gagetown, including a historical review of herbicide use from 1952 to 2005, barrel investigations at 14 sites in 2005–2006, and human-health risk assessments. The official page says the Government of Canada later provided eligible individuals a one-time, tax-free ex gratia payment of $20,000 for possible exposure to unregistered U.S. herbicides between 1966 and 1967.

notable_incidents.description: After a retired CAF member identified an area of interest near the former Shirley Road dump in June 2018, DND says an independent investigation in August 2018 of about 223 hectares identified 105 magnetic anomalies that were excavated. Items found included an ammo box and scrap metal; the official page states no barrels were found and that DND had no plans for further barrel-search activities at that time.

sites.notes: Coordinates are the official NRCan CGNDB military feature 'Gagetown Range and Training Area' (geoname DBDXI), not a surveyed range footprint. A separately named official CGNDB feature 'Canadian Forces Base Gagetown' (DAABL) is at 45.833333, -66.45, nearer the Oromocto garrison described on the base page. Five former waste-disposal sites at the base are described on the Agent Orange investigations page (Shirley Road main dump, drum disposal area, asbestos dump area, chemical container disposal area, and ash disposal site); the chemical container disposal area was excavated and remediated in 1984. Those are contamination/disposal sites, not a current munitions inventory. A 2006 DND-wide herbicide review cited on that page concluded Agent Orange and other unregistered U.S. herbicides were only used at Base Gagetown among the CAF sites reviewed.

sites.known_energetics: A 2015 DRDC article says large-scale blast and weapons trials are conducted on the Experimental Proving Ground (EPG), including historical 1960s trials that used 500 tonnes of TNT, and that weapons-system evaluations (the article names CRV-7 rockets, TOW missiles, various gun systems, and a test of the Excalibur artillery round) have been conducted there. The article also says the EPG supports CBRNE training that can use live agents. This draft does not have a current item-level inventory.
sites.current_status: Active CFB, British Army Training Unit Suffield (BATUS) host, and DRDC Suffield Research Centre Experimental Proving Ground. A 7 October 2026 National Defence news release says CFB Suffield provides training and testing capabilities and hosts BATUS, and announces $750 million for a new Chemical and Biological Laboratory and Blast Assessment Centre at CFB Suffield. A November 2024 National Defence briefing said construction was commencing on a $44 million Neurobehavioral Blast Research Facility of about 1,400 m2 at DRDC Suffield. No open IAAC public-comment period for Suffield was found on 2026-11-23.

notable_incidents.description: The 2015 DRDC article states that in 1941 the Canadian and British governments jointly procured 2,700 square kilometres of land to develop the Suffield Experimental Station (SES), described there as a chemical and biological weapons test facility used during the Second World War for countermeasures testing.
notable_incidents.summary: The 2015 DRDC article states that in 1941 the Canadian and British governments jointly procured 2,700 square kilometres of land to develop the Suffield Experimental Station (SES), described there as a chemical and biological weapons test facility used during the Second World War for countermeasures testing.

notable_incidents.description: On 20 June 2023, the Department of National Defence issued a Notice of Determination under IAAC registry 83455 for upgrades to the existing Range 8 facility at Garrison Wainwright, determining that the project was not likely to cause significant adverse environmental effects. The project description included re-grading of firing positions and bullet stops, screening of sand at bullet stops, demolition and reconstruction of a sentry building, and installation of self-healing membrane liners at bullet stops. Construction had been proposed for July to November 2022.

sites.name: 12 Wing Shearwater — proposed Explosive Ordnance Disposal Range
sites.branch: Department of National Defence / Royal Canadian Navy (Fleet Diving Unit Atlantic) / Royal Canadian Air Force (12 Wing)

sites.coordinate_method: Official CGNDB military or populated-place feature uniquely named for this installation or training area.
sites.known_energetics: The IAAC 90236 project description says the proposed EOD range would include a fenced sand-pit area with a berm for disposal of white phosphorus munitions, a fenced area with dirt or fine gravel and a berm for disposal of other conventional unexploded ordnance, and an operational readiness suite (demolition bunker) made from an intermodal shipping container with protective works. It also states that live ordnance and white phosphorus munitions are currently transported on public roads to 5 CDSB Gagetown for disposal.
sites.current_status: Proposed DND project on federal lands; not confirmed as constructed. IAAC registry 90236 public comments closed on 10 March 2026. As of the registry page checked on 2026-11-23, the assessment status was still 'In progress', and DND was considering comments before determining whether the project is likely to cause significant adverse environmental effects. No determination had been posted, and the comment period was not open.

notable_incidents.description: The public comment period on IAAC registry 90236 (proposed EOD range at 12 Wing Shearwater) closed on 10 March 2026. The official project description states that Joint Task Force Atlantic does not have an EOD range in the Halifax area for munitions tasked for disposal by the Royal Canadian Navy’s Fleet Diving Unit Atlantic, and that live ordnance and white phosphorus munitions are currently transported on public roads to 5 CDSB Gagetown in Oromocto, New Brunswick, for safe disposal. As of 2026-11-23 the assessment remained in progress with no posted determination.
